title: Dalal Street Braces for Blockbuster Week: SBI Funds Debut, Manipal Health IPO, and Five More
excerpt: India's primary market enters its busiest stretch of 2026 with three major listings on Monday, including the ₹9,813 crore SBI Funds Management IPO, while seven new issues prepare to open for subscription.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • SBI Funds Management's IPO drew ₹3 trillion in bids, India's fourth most-subscribed ever.
  • Manipal Health's ₹11,000 crore IPO could become India's largest of 2026.
  • Seven new public issues are set to open this week, signaling market recovery.
  • NRI investors can participate in most mainboard IPOs through demat accounts.

Expected Listing Gain
  • SBI Funds Management, India's largest mutual fund house, lists on Monday July 21 after drawing ₹3 trillion in bids — the country's fourth most-subscribed IPO ever — with grey market premiums signalling a 16% listing gain.
  • Seven new public issues are set to open this week, headlined by Manipal Health's ₹11,000 crore offering — India's biggest IPO of 2026 — and the ₹5,000 crore Cube Highways InvIT.
  • The pipeline includes mainboard issues from Indo-MIM, Xtranet Technologies, and Lohia Corp, alongside ongoing subscription for Caliber Mining and Logistics.
  • NRI investors can participate in most mainboard IPOs through their demat accounts, though the minimum investment for Caliber Mining is ₹14,840 per lot.

Dalal Street is gearing up for what could be its most action-packed week of 2026, with three companies set to make their trading debut on Monday and seven new initial public offerings scheduled to open for subscription. The flurry of activity signals a decisive rebound in India's primary market after a sluggish first half.

The centrepiece is SBI Funds Management, the country's largest mutual fund house, whose ₹9,813 crore IPO drew bids worth a staggering ₹3 trillion ($31.14 billion) — making it India's fourth most-subscribed public offering on record, according to Reuters.

Monday's Triple Listing

Three companies are set to debut on the BSE and NSE on Monday, July 21.

SBI Funds Management, a joint venture between State Bank of India and Europe's largest asset manager Amundi, priced its IPO at ₹574 per share. The issue was subscribed 41.66 times overall, with qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) booking their portion 140 times over. Anchor investors, including BlackRock and sovereign wealth funds from Singapore, Abu Dhabi, and Norway, contributed $278.5 million. Grey market premiums of around ₹92 suggest a potential listing at roughly ₹666, an upside of about 16%, according to Outlook Money.

Alpine Texworld, a mainboard listing with an issue price of ₹105, saw far more modest demand at 1.38 times subscription. Grey market premiums have slumped to ₹2-3, pointing to a listing with marginal gains of roughly 2%.

Millworks Technologies, an SME issue priced at ₹331, was the week's subscription standout, oversubscribed 192.73 times.

New Issues Opening This Week

Caliber Mining and Logistics, which opened for subscription on July 17 at a price band of ₹402-424, closes bidding on Monday. The coal mining and logistics firm aims to raise ₹450 crore through a mix of fresh shares (₹400 crore) and an offer for sale (₹50 crore). As of its first day, the issue was subscribed 1.21 times. The company, which serves Coal India subsidiaries including Western Coalfields and Northern Coalfields, is expected to list on July 24. Grey market premiums signal a potential 24% listing premium, according to Outlook Business.

Cube Highways Trust InvIT opens for subscription on July 22 with a price band of ₹151-152 per unit. The ₹5,000 crore issue — entirely an offer for sale — marks the trust's conversion from a privately listed InvIT to a publicly listed one. The I-Squared Capital-sponsored trust manages 27 operational highway assets spanning 8,754 lane kilometres across 12 states. Premji Invest has committed ₹950 crore, alongside HDFC Life Insurance and Axis Max Life, according to The Hindu BusinessLine.

Xtranet Technologies opens on July 23 with a price band of ₹120-127 per share, seeking ₹170 crore through a fresh issue. The IT solutions provider specialises in enterprise applications, digital transformation, and managed services. Listing is expected on July 30.

Lohia Corp, a global manufacturer of polypropylene and high-density polyethylene machinery, also opens on July 23. The issue consists entirely of an offer for sale of 25.9 million shares by the promoter group.

"Market sentiment remains broadly constructive, supported by improving macroeconomic indicators, favourable liquidity conditions, and rising interest from both institutional and retail investors."

— Bajaj Broking Research

The Manipal Health Mega-IPO

The week's biggest headline, however, belongs to Manipal Health Enterprises. The Temasek-backed hospital chain is targeting a valuation of approximately ₹80,000 crore ($8.3 billion) for its planned IPO, which could launch in the week starting July 27, according to Bloomberg. The company plans to raise as much as ₹11,000 crore through a combination of a fresh issue worth ₹8,000 crore and an offer for sale of 43.23 million shares by existing shareholders including TPG Inc.

If launched as planned, it would become India's largest IPO of 2026, surpassing SBI Funds Management's offering. The targeted valuation is below the $10-12 billion range floated in April, reflecting cautious investor sentiment amid Middle East tensions, Bloomberg reported.

Indo-MIM, Bengaluru-based precision engineering firm and the world's largest manufacturer using metal injection moulding technology, is also expected to open its IPO this week. The company recently halved its fresh issue to ₹500 crore from an initial ₹1,000 crore.

What It Means for NRI Investors

The revival of India's primary market offers NRI investors significant opportunities. SBI Funds Management, as India's largest asset manager overseeing ₹12.5 trillion in assets, provides direct exposure to the country's mutual fund boom. Meanwhile, Cube Highways offers a play on India's expanding highway infrastructure.

For those tracking the healthcare sector, Manipal Health — with 38 hospitals and over 10,761 licensed beds across 14 states — represents one of the most consequential healthcare listings in Indian market history.

What's Next

India is set for a packed pipeline of public offerings in the second half of 2026, with mega listings from Reliance Jio and the National Stock Exchange expected before year-end, according to Reuters. The success of SBI Funds Management's IPO — which marked a strong comeback for India's primary market — suggests institutional appetite for quality Indian assets remains robust.

Upcoming IPOs This Week

›Cube Highways InvIT: ₹5,000 crore
›Caliber Mining: ₹450 crore, subscribed 1.21 times
›Xtranet Technologies: ₹170 crore, opens July 23
